item.title: CPR Center for Performance Research: Artist-in-Residence Program 2027
item.description:
Organisation: CPR - Center for Performance Research

Location: Brooklyn, New York City, USA. RESTRICTED: NYC-based artists only; CPR does not sponsor visas, and residents must remain NYC-based for the whole cycle.

Award: $2,000 stipend, 20 free hours of rehearsal space, up to 150 subsidised rehearsal hours across CPR's two studios with priority and advance booking, presentation slots in the OPEN LAB and OPEN AiR programmes, and access to technical equipment and production support. No application fee.

Duration: One year, January to December 2027

Deadline: Closed 24 Aug 2026

CPR's year-long Artist-in-Residence programme supports six New York City-based artists working across contemporary dance, performance and time-based art. The organisation values experimental approaches to content, form and aesthetics and explicitly encourages risk-taking, interdisciplinarity and the unexpected, so process-led and hard-to-categorise work is in scope rather than a liability. WHAT RESIDENTS RECEIVE: a $2,000 stipend; 20 free hours of rehearsal space plus up to 150 further subsidised hours in CPR's two studios, with priority and advance calendar access; participation in OPEN LAB (facilitated embodied workshops and feedback showings) and OPEN AiR (solo or shared presentations of current work); and access to technical equipment and production support. ELIGIBILITY: artists must be based in New York City and remain so throughout the cycle (no visa sponsorship); must have had work publicly presented before; must not have held a CPR residency in the last five years; and current undergraduates are not eligible. Individuals, companies, collaboratives and collectives may all apply, each counting as a single residency. CPR strongly encourages applications from BIPOC, LGBTQ+, immigrant and disabled artists and from artists across generations. APPLICATION: a Google Form with narrative answers on the artist's central research focus and its alignment with CPR's values; drafting answers in a separate document first is recommended. Selection is by an independent panel of artists, curators and arts leaders. Deadline: Monday 24 August 2026 at 5pm ET; late submissions are not accepted. Notifications November 2026. Questions: applications@cprnyc.org.

item.title: Teiger Foundation: Hosting Grant (September 2026 quarterly deadline)
item.description:
Organisation: Teiger Foundation

Location: United States. The presenting organisation must be US-based, though the originating project may have come from anywhere in the world.

Award: USD 50,000 or USD 75,000 (fixed request tiers, applicant chooses). Up to 30 percent may cover indirect and overhead costs. Organisations with annual budgets under USD 3.5 million receive special consideration for infrastructure costs. No matching requirement. No application fee.

Duration: Roughly 12 months; the 9 September 2026 deadline covers projects opening between 1 April 2027 and 31 March 2028.

Deadline: 09 Sep 2026

Funds US organisations to present curator-led contemporary visual art exhibitions and projects that originated elsewhere, on condition the presenting institution meaningfully adapts the project to its own context. Teiger's remit covers group exhibitions, single-artist surveys, participatory and community-engaged projects, digital exhibitions, and live and virtual performance, making it one of very few US funders that will directly finance media-art and performance programming at organisational level. Requests are fixed at USD 50,000 or USD 75,000 with up to 30 percent for indirect costs, and there is no minimum organisation budget size, with smaller organisations explicitly favoured for infrastructure support. Hosting deadlines are quarterly: 9 September 2026 and 9 December 2026, both 17:00 ET, each mapped to a defined project-opening window roughly a year out. IMPORTANT: re-presenting a touring project unchanged is explicitly not competitive; the curatorial adaptation is the substance of the application. US 501(c)(3) status is required and the fund is not open to individuals or non-US organisations. Teiger's larger biennial Call for Proposals is not running in 2026 and next opens in autumn 2026 with an early-2027 deadline.

Open call details

item.title: Andy Warhol Foundation: Exhibition Support (Fall 2026 round)
item.description:
Organisation: The Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts

Location: Applicant's own venue. US-based 501(c)(3) required; international organisations must first submit a letter of inquiry before any proposal is accepted.

Award: USD 60,000 to 100,000. Direct costs only (artist payments, catalogue and publication, artist-designed public programmes); staff salaries excluded. Request must not exceed 25 percent of total direct project costs, which functions as a de facto 75 percent co-financing requirement. No application fee.

Duration: Exhibition must open between 6 months and 2 years after notification.

Deadline: 01 Sep 2026

Supports solo, two-person and thematic group exhibitions of contemporary visual art. The Foundation explicitly prioritises artists whose work is under-recognised and whose practices are experimental or hard to categorise, which makes it a genuine route for media arts, digital culture and art-and-science exhibitions rather than a blue-chip-only fund. Grants of USD 60,000 to 100,000 cover direct exhibition costs including artist fees, new commissions, catalogue production and artist-designed public programming, but not staff salaries. Applicants may request no more than 25 percent of total direct costs. The proposal is a roughly three-page curatorial letter plus detailed direct-cost budget, organisational budget and IRS documentation. Deadlines are 1 March and 1 September annually, with notifications 1 July and 1 January. IMPORTANT: this is a postmark or email-timestamp deadline, not a portal deadline. Fiscal sponsors are explicitly not accepted; the applicant must hold its own IRS ruling letter. The six-month-to-two-year timing rule is strict, so a September 2026 application suits exhibitions programmed from mid-2027 onward.

Open call details

item.title: Andy Warhol Foundation: Project Grants for Small-Scale Organizations (Fall 2026 round)
item.description:
Organisation: The Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts

Location: Applicant's own venue or programme, with a mandatory public component. US-based only.

Award: USD 20,000 to 30,000 toward direct costs such as artist payments and production. No application fee.

Duration: Project must complete within one year of notification; September-round projects may begin 1 January 2027 or later.

Deadline: 01 Sep 2026

Launched in February 2026 as an expansion of the Foundation's programme to reach organisations too small for the Exhibition Support and Multi-year strands, and it is the single most relevant new US scheme for small media-arts festivals. It funds visual arts projects with a public component, explicitly naming film festivals, exhibitions, installations, residencies and interdisciplinary collaborations. Grants are USD 20,000 to 30,000 toward direct costs. The hard gate is the USD 200,000 annual operating budget ceiling plus US 501(c)(3) status held directly by the applicant, not via a fiscal sponsor. The Foundation states it assesses creative risk-taking and the growth of participating artists rather than community impact metrics, which suits experimental sound and digital culture programming. Proposals are a maximum of three pages plus a one-year operating budget, a project budget and IRS documentation. Deadlines are 1 March (projects begin 1 July or later) and 1 September (projects begin 1 January or later). Youth-focused projects are ineligible. One project per round, and grantees must wait a year after project completion and final reporting before reapplying.

item.title: Wave Hill: 2027 Sunroom Project Space (NYC)
item.description:
Organisation: Wave Hill

Location: Glyndor Gallery, Wave Hill, the Bronx, New York City, USA. For early-career artists living within a 50-mile radius of the Bronx.

Award: $2,000 honorarium per artist, plus exhibition and professional development support, a co-designed Meet the Artist public program, and a short exhibition essay published in print and online. Four artists selected. No application fee.

Duration: Nine to twelve months of research and development leading to a solo presentation during the 2027 season

Deadline: Closed 09 Aug 2026

The Sunroom Project Space gives artists in the New York City area who are in the early stages of their careers, regardless of age, the chance to develop and show a site-specific solo project in the Sunroom or Sun Porch of Glyndor Gallery at Wave Hill. For the 2027 season, Wave Hill is especially interested in projects that recognise ancestral wisdom in relation to our connection with the earth and soil: practices, beliefs and values passed down through generations, particularly those that foster harmonious relationships with our ecosystems, for example regenerative farming and agricultural practices and the care of soil, water and plant life. Projects engaging the history of earth or land art (concepts, materials, sites and relationships to place) that intersect with sustainable practices and ancestral wisdom are also welcome. AWARD: four artists are selected for solo presentations, each receiving a $2,000 honorarium, exhibition and professional development support, and nine to twelve months to research and develop their ideas. Each project is accompanied by a Meet the Artist program co-designed with the artist, and a short exhibition essay published in print and online. ELIGIBILITY: artists working across media, in the early stages of their career regardless of education, living within a 50-mile radius of the Bronx. Not eligible: students enrolled in a degree-granting program; artists with commercial gallery representation; artists who have previously exhibited a site-specific project at Wave Hill; artists who participated in the 2026 Winter Workspace program at Wave Hill. Applications are reviewed by a jury of Wave Hill's Curator of Visual Arts, an invited guest curator and a prior 2026 Sunroom Project Space artist. An online information session is held Monday 13 July, 12-1PM; RSVP to visualarts@wavehill.org with the subject line '2027 Sunroom Project Space Info Session'. DEADLINE: 9 August 2026. Apply via SlideRoom.

Open call details

The QM-Jerome Foundation Fellowship for Emerging Artists selects two emerging visual artists living in New York City for its 2027-2028 cohort. Each fellow receives a $20,000 award, professional development consultations, mentorship from Queens Museum staff and an established New York-based artist, and a solo exhibition at the Queens Museum in 2028, with curatorial support across a full year of project development. Aimed at early-career visual artists (roughly two to ten years of professional practice) who have a consistent practice and developing public profile but have not yet reached major institutional recognition. ELIGIBILITY: must currently reside in one of NYC's five boroughs and maintain residency through the fellowship; artists enrolled in degree-granting programs are not eligible; review the detailed criteria on exhibition history, previous grants and years of practice. Supported by the Jerome Foundation. Apply via the Queens Museum fellowship program page. Deadline: 28 September 2026, 11:59 PM EST.

item.title: City of Moorhead: 2026 Call for Public Art (Movable Interactive Piece)
item.description:
Organisation: City of Moorhead, Minnesota

Location: Moorhead, Minnesota, USA. The piece will be sited at different locations throughout the city. No geographic eligibility restriction is stated in the call, so non-US artists appear eligible, but this is not confirmed in writing.

Award: Not published. The call announcement states no budget, commission amount or artist fee, and the linked Request for Art document could not be retrieved. Confirm the budget with art@moorheadmn.gov before investing time in a proposal. No application fee is mentioned.

Duration: Single commission; timeline not published

Deadline: 04 Sep 2026

The City of Moorhead is seeking proposals for an inspirational, movable public artwork to be installed at rotating locations across the city. Interactive elements are explicitly encouraged, with kinetic sculpture, digital installation and tactile elements named as examples. Strong proposals invite public participation, promote creativity and youth engagement, are safe for all members of the public, are durable enough for year-round outdoor conditions, and draw people to gather. Submissions are reviewed and ranked by the Artist Review Team, whose recommendation passes to the Art and Culture Commission and then to City Council for the final decision. Questions go to art@moorheadmn.gov. Proposals are due by 10:00am on Friday 4 September 2026.

item.title: The Gallery at Penn College: 2027-28 Call for Exhibitions
item.description:
Organisation: The Gallery at Penn College (Pennsylvania College of Technology)

Location: Williamsport, Pennsylvania, USA, on the Pennsylvania College of Technology campus. Travel note: Williamsport Regional Airport connects only to Washington Dulles, with no other direct flights or trains, so international travel involves a connection. No nationality restriction is stated.

Award: Housing, meals, a solo exhibition honorarium, and a shipping and travel stipend are all provided. Specific figures are not published in the call. No application fee is stated.

Duration: Exhibition slot within the 2027-28 season; review takes place during autumn semester with artists notified in January

Deadline: 31 Aug 2026

The Gallery at Penn College is accepting proposals for solo, two-person and group exhibitions in its 2027-28 season. All entries are juried through a blind selection process by a gallery committee of faculty, staff, K-12 art educators and community artists. The space is 3,000 square feet with 82 to 250 running feet of linear wall depending on configuration and a ceiling height of 11 feet 4 inches, and all exhibitions are installed by gallery staff. Site-specific installations requiring artist installation need an approved planning document first. Campus visits are a valued part of programming though some exhibitions are scheduled without one; visiting artists give a 20 to 30 minute gallery talk at the public reception, and are encouraged to propose class-specific programmes or community workshops. Promotional support includes an annual gallery catalogue, postcards, press releases and web and social coverage. Applications require 10 to 15 digital images (JPG only, max 4 MB each), an image list with dimensions and medium, a CV and an artist statement.

item.title: Wave Hill / AnkhLave Arts Alliance: 2027 Van Lier Fellowship (NYC)
item.description:
Organisation: Wave Hill / AnkhLave Arts Alliance

Location: Wave Hill Public Garden and Cultural Center, the Bronx, New York City, USA. For NYC-based BIPOC visual artists aged 30 or younger.

Award: $10,435 stipend, including an $8,000 honorarium, a transportation stipend for the residency, and professional development opportunities, plus the Winter Workspace residency, a solo exhibition with public programs, mentorship from Wave Hill curatorial staff and arts professionals, and AnkhLave Alumni Network benefits. Two fellowships awarded. No application fee.

Duration: January to December 2027; Winter Workspace residency 23 February - 18 April 2027; solo exhibition 15 May - 4 July 2027

Deadline: Closed 10 Aug 2026

Wave Hill, in partnership with AnkhLave Arts Alliance, invites NYC-based artists who identify as BIPOC to apply for the 2027 Van Lier Fellowship as part of the 9th Annual AnkhLave Garden Project at Wave Hill Public Garden and Cultural Center in the Bronx. The project supports artists who draw on research, scholarship and lived knowledge to present site-responsive work at the intersection of nature, culture and place, engaging with Wave Hill's plant collections, history, design and architecture. The Van Lier Fellowship (funded by the Edward and Sally Van Lier Fund through the New York Community Trust) will be awarded to two NYC-based visual artists aged 30 or younger. FELLOWSHIP: participation in the Winter Workspace residency (23 February - 18 April 2027); a $10,435 stipend including an $8,000 honorarium and transportation stipend; a solo exhibition in the Sunroom or Sun Porch (15 May - 4 July 2027); public engagement through Winter Workspace programming and a Meet the Artist program; mentorship with Wave Hill curatorial staff, working artists and arts professionals; and AnkhLave Alumni Network benefits. ELIGIBILITY: emerging artists 30 or younger (born 1997 or after) from historically underrepresented communities; live in one of the five NYC boroughs; demonstrate financial need; have completed college and not be enrolled in a degree-granting program during the residency; not represented by a commercial gallery; available for both programs; cannot have been a Van Lier Fellow elsewhere or have previously done a Winter Workspace residency or exhibited at Wave Hill or with AnkhLave. Works may not include nudity, depictions of violence or profanity. Artists may apply to only one of the two 2027 AnkhLave Garden Project opportunities. Questions: visualarts@wavehill.org with '2027 Van Lier-Ankhlave' in the subject. DEADLINE: 10 August 2026. Apply via SlideRoom.

item.title: JCAL: ARTWorks Fellowship 2026-2027
item.description:
Organisation: Jamaica Center for Arts and Learning (JCAL)

Location: Jamaica, Queens, New York City, USA. Open to visual artists based in New York City (preferably Queens) or Long Island; priority to Queens-based BIIPOC artists.

Award: $5,000 per Fellow, paid out over the course of the program, plus free shared studio space at JCAL (about 550 sq ft, as available), a 7 x 4 ft storage closet, one free JCAL class (space-available), an Artist Mentor and seminar series, and a concluding two-month group exhibition with catalogue in JCAL's Miller and Community galleries. No application fee.

Duration: Six-month fellowship: 7 October 2026 to 18 June 2027; exhibition opens 9 April 2027

Deadline: Closed 13 Jul 2026

Jamaica Center for Arts and Learning (JCAL) invites New York City-based visual artists to apply for ARTWorks, its Artist Fellowship Training Seminar Series: a six-month fellowship focused on career sustainability that amplifies the work of emerging, underrepresented visual artists. Six Fellows treat their practice as a small business, set entrepreneurial and professional goals, and build a long-term plan, supported by a Program Manager, an established Artist Mentor, cohort meetings, and at least six seminar events (past topics: copyright and contracts, working with galleries and collectors, grant writing, taxes and accounting, marketing, art handling). SUPPORT: $5,000 per Fellow paid over the program, free shared studio space (about 550 sq ft, as available) with a storage closet, one free JCAL class, and a concluding two-month group exhibition with catalogue (opens 9 April 2027). ELIGIBILITY: reside in New York City (preferably Queens) or Long Island; identify as BIIPOC (Black, Immigrant, Indigenous, People of Color); demonstrate clarity of concept and strong craft with a deep commitment to social practice; must NOT have received major exposure via exhibitions, grants or residencies; must not be enrolled in any college degree or certificate program; past Fellows ineligible. Priority to Queens-based artists of underrepresented communities; multidisciplinary practices welcome, but the program focuses on visual artists working in traditional forms. APPLY via Submittable with six images OR two 3-5 minute videos, a one-page work-sample description, artist statement (max 300 words), one professional reference (max 300 words), CV, and a paragraph on your expectations of ARTWorks. Jury reviews submissions without obvious identifiers. TIMELINE: first-round notifications 3 August 2026, interviews 11-14 August, Fellows notified 21 August, program runs 7 October 2026 to 18 June 2027. DEADLINE: midnight Monday 13 July 2026 (portal closes 14 July 2026, 6:00 AM ET).

Open call details

item.title: Wassaic Project 2027 Summer Exhibition Open Call
item.description:
Organisation: The Wassaic Project

Location: Wassaic, New York, United States (in and around historic Wassaic and Maxon Mills).

Award: A modest honorarium for all accepted artists (part of the organization's effort toward W.A.G.E. certification). Artists creating site-specific installations are also eligible for an Exhibitions Fellowship and a no-fee residency of 1-4 weeks in April or May 2027.

Duration: The 2027 Summer Exhibition runs free and open to the public every weekend, 1 May to 12 September 2027. Optional fellowship residency of 1-4 weeks in April or May 2027.

Deadline: Closed 10 Aug 2026

The Wassaic Project is holding its annual Open Call for the 2027 Summer Exhibition, for artists of all mediums, including 2D work, sculpture, video, new media, site-specific installation, performance, text, poems, essays, and publication-specific work. Selected work is showcased alongside a diverse range of pieces and performances in and around historic Wassaic and Maxon Mills; the 2027 Summer Exhibition will be free and open to the public every weekend from 1 May to 12 September 2027. In an effort toward W.A.G.E. certification, all accepted artists receive a modest honorarium to participate. Artists interested in creating a site-specific installation are also eligible for an Exhibitions Fellowship to help realize their work; Fellows are offered a no-fee residency for 1-4 weeks in April or May 2027 (artists interested in making site-specific work should still apply regardless of whether they are interested in or able to be in residence). The Wassaic Project cultivates and supports community for emerging and professional contemporary artists, writers, and other creatives, with a residency program housed in historic landmark buildings that hosts 10 artists each month in the heart of a rural community. APPLICATION: requires application forms, a CV, and an artwork/portfolio; submitted via SlideRoom. Application fee: USD 25 (no participation fee or additional fees). Deadline 10 August 2026.

item.title: Pioneer Works: 2027 Open Call – Visual Arts and Music Residency (Brooklyn, NY)
item.description:
Organisation: Pioneer Works

Location: Pioneer Works, Red Hook, Brooklyn, New York, USA

Award: Visual Arts: USD 5,000 one-time award (USD 2,500 honorarium + USD 500/month stipend for 5 months). Music: USD 3,000 one-time award (USD 2,500 honorarium + USD 500/month stipend for 1 month). Free studio space and facilities access. No housing or travel provided. No application fee.

Duration: Visual Arts: 5 months. Music: 1 month. Cohort begins after jury decisions in late September 2026.

Deadline: Closed 17 Jul 2026

Pioneer Works in Red Hook, Brooklyn invites applications from emerging visual artists and musicians for its 2027 residency cohort. 12 Visual Arts residents (5-month residency) and 12 Music residents (1-month residency) are selected each year through a two-phase jury process. WHAT IS PROVIDED: free studio space; access to facilities including risograph printer, darkroom, ceramics studio, large-format printer, 3D printers, thermobinder, and laser cutter; biweekly studio visits with curators, gallerists, critics, and artists; free access to all public programmes at Pioneer Works, including Second Sundays (monthly open studios and performances). FINANCIAL AWARD: USD 5,000 for Visual Arts residents; USD 3,000 for Music residents (each comprising a USD 2,500 honorarium plus USD 500/month for the residency duration); applicants' choice on how to spend it. Pioneer Works does not provide housing, travel, or visa sponsorship. ELIGIBILITY: open locally, nationally, and internationally; collectives may apply (resources shared); current students and programme alumni are not eligible. REVIEW PROCESS: phase one is internal scoring on technical ability, uniqueness of vision, and future potential (nontraditional career paths given special consideration); highest scorers advance to an external jury of art professionals and alumni who assess diversity of demographics and media, genuine studio need, and fit with Pioneer Works' public-facing culture. Jury convenes September 2026; all applicants notified by late September. Supported by Dalio Philanthropies, the Andy Warhol Foundation, NYC Department of Cultural Affairs, New York State Council on the Arts, and the National Endowment for the Arts. APPLY: via Pioneer Works website by 17 July 2026 (extended). Questions: residency@pioneerworks.org.

item.description:
Organisation: Shelley & Donald Rubin Foundation (The 8th Floor)

Location: The 8th Floor, near Union Square, New York City, United States

Award: Fixed artist fees: $300 for a group screening; $500 for a solo screening; $750 for a solo performance, with an additional $250 for reimbursable production costs (collaborators, materials, transportation, rehearsal, specific AV/lighting beyond the gallery inventory). For duos and collectives the fees are shared. The primary applicant must be able to submit an invoice and US tax form to receive payment. No application fee.

Duration: 2026/27 programming season at The 8th Floor

Deadline: Closed 05 Jul 2026

Seventh season of Sight/Geist, a series from the Shelley & Donald Rubin Foundation supporting emerging NYC-based film and performance artists. The Foundation provides curatorial, administrative and promotional support, plus documentation for performances and discussions; selected artists also engage in a Q&A on their broader practice. TWO CATEGORIES: (1) single-channel screening - experimental/non-commercial cinema, video art or performance documentation as a single-channel non-looped projection with 2.1 PA; H.264 or ProRes; under 80 minutes (priority to <20 min); (2) performance and expanded forms - 20-50 minutes; may foreground duration, movement, audiovisual media, voice, site specificity, audience participation; conceptual and political proposals encouraged. ELIGIBILITY: primary applicant must be at least 18 and maintain their primary residence in New York City (or spend most of their artistic, professional and social life in NYC); self-identify as an 'emerging' artist (early-career, self-trained, newly graduated, or currently enrolled in undergraduate/graduate programs); one submission per artist/duo/collective. Submissions open 1 June through 11 pm ET, 5 July 2026; applicants notified by late August 2026. Contact: info@the8thfloor.org.

item.title: The Lab: Living Wage Residencies 2026-27 (San Francisco)
item.description:
Organisation: The Lab

Location: San Francisco Bay Area, California, USA (eligibility restricted to artists based in the Bay Area; significant in-person access to The Lab's space in the Mission District is required)

Award: USD 17,530 artist fee per resident (commensurate with three months of work at a San Francisco Bay Area living wage per MIT's Living Wage Calculator) plus USD 5,000 for collaborators and materials. Three months of rehearsal/workshop access to The Lab's space, plus two weeks of continuous use of the exhibition and performance spaces for the residency outcome. Curatorial and marketing support, outside studio visits, documentation and publicity. Stage-2 finalists receive an additional USD 250 stipend to develop their full proposal. No application fee.

Duration: Residencies take place between July 2026 and June 2027

Deadline: Closed 31 May 2026

The Lab's flagship Living Wage Residency, a substantial in-person residency in San Francisco's Mission District for artists working in any media and discipline. Since 2014 the programme has directed over USD 1 million to artists, with artist fees representing nearly 30% of The Lab's average operating budget. The Lab's history is as a site for experimental and interdisciplinary work spanning performance, exhibition, installation, sound and experimental music, writing, institutional critique, social practice, parades, feasts and further disciplines yet to be defined. The Lab's mission centres traditionally underrepresented artists, particularly those identifying as BIPOC, LGBTQ+, women, disabled and/or from economically marginalised backgrounds. ELIGIBILITY: artists based in the San Francisco Bay Area (tight geographic restriction; in-person access to The Lab's space is central to the residency). SUPPORT per residency: USD 17,530 artist fee (3 months at a Bay Area living wage per MIT's Living Wage Calculator); USD 5,000 for collaborators and materials; three months of rehearsal/workshop access to The Lab's space (as available around other programming); two weeks of continuous use of the exhibition and performance spaces; curatorial and marketing support, outside studio visits, documentation and publicity. PROCESS: Stage 1 application (CV, 3 work links, brief project description and resource plan) due 31 May 2026; Stage 2 invites up to 12 selected artists to develop a full proposal with a USD 250 stipend (Stage 2 deadline TBD). Reviewed by a diverse panel of professional artists and curators plus The Lab's Board. Outside funding additionally secured for a proposal is not factored into the decision, but The Lab may help identify further sources. Supported by the San Francisco Arts Commission.

item.title: MTA Arts & Design Digital Art Program 2026 Open Call
item.description:
Organisation: MTA Arts & Design

Location: New York City, USA (Fulton Transit Center, Grand Central Madison, Moynihan Train Hall)

Award: $1,000 honorarium for finalist proposals + project budget for selected artist(s) (TBD by project nature)

Duration: Up to 2-minute works on display ~3 months in 2027

Deadline: Closed 28 May 2026

Open call for digital and new-media artists to submit existing works for consideration on transit-center screens (video, film, animation, augmented reality, net art, game engines, generative art). Multi-channel installation experience encouraged. Finalists develop site-specific proposals with a $1,000 honorarium; selected artists oversee production and installation with project management from MTA Arts & Design. Sites have no audio. Valid U.S. Taxpayer ID required. Submit up to 5 works (.mov/.mp4) and 10 stills (.jpg/.png) plus bio, CV and artist statement. Deadline 23:59 EST Thursday 28 May 2026.
